messages:
maria: Planning: Wed 03:00-07:00 UTC maintenance for us-east1 -- livepatch kernel + nvme firmware. We'll do 6 cohorts of ~4 nodes (~32 GPUs) every 30m, scoped per-AZ to avoid cross-AZ egress spikes.

sam: What's the expected effective capacity hit during the rollout?

maria: Peak expected ~6-9% GPU capacity reduction while cohort drains. With throttles and pacing we expect p99 to stay within the 250ms SLO.

anya: Any special steps for IO-heavy tenants (large batch embedding jobs)? Last firmware roll caused job retries.

maria: We'll apply a tenant-level policy to deprioritize batch jobs: routing weight=0.3 for batch tags and set max-concurrency=1 for non-prod. We'll also flag tenants that do heavy IO so support can notify.

rui: Can we avoid on-demand spillover to other regions? Egress caps last time were painful.

maria: Plan is AZ-scoped cohorts (us-east1-b then -c then -a), and we'll enable local burst first. If overflow is unavoidable fallback to eu-west1 read-only endpoints for non-critical traffic only. ops will publish the capacity thresholds that trigger fallback.

eng-oncall-bot: Maintenance scheduled: us-east1 kernel livepatch + NVMe fw, start=1725082800 (Wed 03:00 UTC), end=1725097200 (Wed 07:00 UTC), cohorts=6 x ~30m. Automated canary: rack-11, rack-14.

maria: Runbook excerpt (paste here for oncall):

```
# cordon/drain with careful eviction of large-io pods
kubectl cordon <node>
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --pod-selector='app!=priority' --grace-period=180
# after reboot, run KV pre-seed and io-smoke checks
kubectl apply -f kvcache-seed.yaml -n runtime
python infra-automation/scripts/io_smoke_check.py --node <node> --prefix_tokens 8000
```

sam: Add a gate after cohort-2: run io-smoke-check and generator latency smoke. If latency regresses >15% pause rollout.

maria: Gate added. infra-automation will block the next cohort via the CI job if checks fail.

infra-automation: Note: automation will push cohort status to #maint-status and to the ops status page. We'll also emit a machine-readable event for the canary results.

anya: Cost impact? Finance will want a ballpark for potential on-demand overflow and customer credits risk.

maria: Estimated delta: baseline risk ~1.5k USD if we offload limited traffic east->eu for 4h; worst-case up to ~2.2k if we hit sustained overflow. Customer credits exposure minimal if we keep throttles.

ops: We'll prepare a customer-facing banner and targeted emails to Dedicated customers who have >5% usage in us-east1. Draft to be sent Tue 17:00 UTC.

rui: Rollback plan?

maria: Stop further drains, uncordon most recently drained node(s) if needed, cancel livepatch job, and move routing weights back to pre-window snapshot. Full rollback steps are in the runbook link (internal).

sam: Who owns verifying NVMe SMART pre-checks and post-checks? We need to ensure firmware write success.

maria: infra-automation owns pre/post SMART checks. They'll run smartctl and report pass/fail. If firmware write fails, the automation will mark cohort as failed and initiate rollback.

eng-oncall-bot: Reminder: Pager escalation unchanged. See #maint-status for live updates.

ops: Confirmed we'll publish the status page, send emails, and tag the support playbook with tenant names for targeted comms.

maria: Final checklist before window: 1) confirm canary racks health, 2) pre-run SMART checks, 3) publish routing throttle rules, 4) infra-automation smoke gate enabled, 5) ops customer comms live.

anya: I'll notify platform teams with heavy IO workloads to reschedule big runs.

sam: :thumbsup:

maria: Will update thread if schedule shifts.
